notes:
High-level: SaaS CX platform focused on automated KB-first support. Customer wants hosted API for velocity — no on-prem.

What they care about:
- Indexing scale: currently ~1.2M canonical docs, expect growth to 2.5M in 12 months.
- Query profile: very chatty UI + background similarity searches -> peak QPS high (target 2.5k-3.5k QPS), tail latency sensitive.
- Reranking: using coarse embedding NN + small cross-encoder reranker. Looking to push reranker to hosted Redwood service if latency allows.
- Latency targets: p95 < 120ms for vector lookup + rerank combined; p99 < 250ms preferred.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget; unit cost must be predictable under sustained high QPS.

Quotes / paraphrases:
- "We can tolerate slightly higher median latency as long as p95 is consistent." — Alex Monroe (Head of Platform).
- "Need a clear failure mode if dedicated throughput is exhausted; can’t degrade to 10s of seconds." — CS lead.
summary_requirements: Index size: 1.2M docs now, planning to 2.5M
Architecture: embedding store + ANN (via hosted) + short cross-encoder reranker
Budget: mid-market predictable spend; ARR target 50k-150k
arch_notes: Plan: use hosted_api for embeddings + ANN endpoint; use Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching and KV caching; consider compact quantized reranker variant for lower latency.
poc_plan: Week1: ingest 500k sample; Week2: 10k QPS synthetic; Week3: reranker latency tuning with quantized model; deliver cost model by end of POC.
procurement_notes: Prefers annual commit if SLOs met. Legal has standard SaaS addendum; data residency flagged for EU customers (they serve EU customers).
deal_risk: medium - technical fit looks good but legal/SAML and cost model clarity required
why_redwood: Liked unified runtime + Optimize tooling; strong batching and KV cache features appealed. Also liked transparent perf/price tradeoffs in the demo.
